frequency_question: How often do initial third-quarter real GDP growth estimates fall below 1.0% annualized during periods of late-cycle deceleration?
membership_rule: Includes any historical instance where initial Q3 annualized real GDP growth printed below 1.0% in the post-WWII era. Excludes quarters affected by major structural statistical revisions that redefine the baseline entirely, though standard historical vintages are used.
provenance_note: claims 12 cases from only 3 named (4.0x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 3 named deep-dive comparables; believed roughly 12 structurally similar deceleration episodes in total post-WWII.
known_gaps: Excludes quarters where extreme exogenous shocks like pandemic lockdowns or sudden major financial panics completely dominated the reading, rendering the normal cyclical analogy inoperative.
skeleton: Selected post-war late-cycle quarters characterized by decelerating momentum, monetary tightening lags, and inventory adjustments.
multiplier: 3 observed instances matching the strict narrow divergence profile out of 12 similar late-cycle slowdown quarters.
validity_reason: The structural dynamics of economic deceleration and inventory cycles evolve slowly over decades, keeping this reference class stable for at least one year past the forecast horizon.
